rationale: design-import-refactor: generic change landed in Pulp per owner decision 2026-10-04; Vellum inherits (see inheritance ledger); inline encoded image bytes (an ImageView data:image source, a SceneImage blob) decoded and uploaded a fresh texture on every Skia paint. Canvas gains draw_image_from_keyed_data[_rect] taking a SHA-256 content key; the base forwards to the unkeyed draw so CoreGraphics and recording backends are unchanged. SkiaCanvas keeps keyed images in an ImageFileCache pool separate from the file-path pool, keyed by content digest and backend and never by buffer address, bounded by a byte budget (retained encoded copy plus decoded or uploaded pixels) with least-recently-used eviction; an image larger than the budget is drawn uncached, so inline images cannot evict file images. Cached frames are pixel-identical to uncached ones. No design-import, Chromium, rendering, packaging, or source-authority boundary moves.
tests: ctest --test-dir build -R 'An inline image larger than the byte budget'
ctest --test-dir build -R 'Disabling the image cache rebuilds keyed inline bytes'
ctest --test-dir build -R 'ImageView data URI decodes once across Graphite paints'
ctest --test-dir build -R 'Inline pool stays within its byte budget'
ctest --test-dir build -R 'Many inline images leave file-image hits untouched'
ctest --test-dir build -R 'Recording canvas records keyed inline bytes'
ctest --test-dir build -R 'SceneImage encoded bytes decode once across Graphite paints'
